title_zh: 具有血凝素柄的粘膜 疫苗接种 为小鼠提供针对流感病毒亚型的广泛保护
source_body_en: Influenza viruses continually evolve through antigenic drift and shift, spreading via respiratory droplets and aerosols. Developing a universal nasal vaccine is essential for preventing seasonal and pandemic infections by inducing long-lasting immunity in the respiratory tract. The neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) transfers IgG Abs across the epithelial barrier. This study investigates whether the i.n. delivery of the conserved Stalk antigen of HA, utilizing the FcRn, can stimulate protective immune responses against various influenza virus subtypes. We engineered a monomeric IgG Fc fused to a modified HA Stalk in its prefusion form. immunized with Stalk-Fc exhibited significant protection against infections from H1N1, H5N1, H6N2, and H9N2 compared with groups of control mice. The immunized mice produced long-lasting HA Stalk–specific IgA and IgG Abs in nasal washes, bronchoalveolar lavage, and blood, along with tissue-resident memory T cells in the lungs and long-lived plasma cells in the bone marrow. This led to notably lower viral replication in the nasal turbinate and lungs. The Stalk-specific Abs demonstrated strong cross-reactivity against different influenza subtypes through neutralization, Ab- or complement-dependent cellular cytotoxicity, or phagocytosis. These results indicate that FcRn efficiently transports HA Stalk-Fc across the respiratory epithelial barrier, supporting the development of a universal influenza nasal vaccine.

title: Emergence of a distinct evolutionary cluster of clade 2.3.4.4b H5 viruses in China during 2024-2025 with rapid evolution and antigenic divergence.
abstract: Clade 2.3.4.4b H5 viruses have undergone continuous evolution since their emergence in China, but the extent of genetic and antigenic diversification among recently circulating viruses remains unclear. Here, we characterized 18 H5 viruses isolated through routine surveillance in China during 2024-2025, together with publicly available clade 2.3.4.4b H5 sequences collected since 2020. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that these isolates formed a distinct evolutionary cluster within clade 2.3.4.4b, designated the G2-derived emerging cluster (G2-EC), which emerged around mid-2024 and exhibited clear genetic divergence from previously circulating H5N1 viruses. G2-EC viruses accumulated a characteristic set of hemagglutinin amino acid substitutions, most of which were located in antigenic regions. Across the clade 2.3.4.4b H5 virus population, the estimated mean HA evolutionary rate was higher during 2024-2025 than during preceding periods. These genetic changes were accompanied by marked antigenic divergence from the Re14 vaccine strain, with 4- to 32-fold reductions in HI titres. Genomic analysis revealed acquisition of PB1 segment from a distinct genetic background in G2-EC H5N1 viruses, followed by the emergence of H5N6 viruses sharing a highly similar genetic backbone but carrying a distinct NA segment, indicating sequential reassortment. Animal experiments showed that representative G2-EC viruses retained high pathogenicity and efficient direct-contact transmission in SPF chickens, while exhibiting relatively limited lethality in mice. Collectively, these findings document a recent evolutionary transition of clade 2.3.4.4b H5 viruses in China, characterized by genetic and antigenic divergence accompanied by sequential reassortment, underscoring the need for continued genomic and antigenic surveillance.

title_zh: 2024-2025 年期间,中国出现了具有快速 进化 和抗原分歧的 2.3.4.4b H5 病毒的独特进化簇。
source_body_en: Clade 2.3.4.4b H5 viruses have undergone continuous evolution since their emergence in China, but the extent of genetic and antigenic diversification among recently circulating viruses remains unclear. Here, we characterized 18 H5 viruses isolated through routine surveillance in China during 2024-2025, together with publicly available clade 2.3.4.4b H5 sequences collected since 2020. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that these isolates formed a distinct evolutionary cluster within clade 2.3.4.4b, designated the G2-derived emerging cluster (G2-EC), which emerged around mid-2024 and exhibited clear genetic divergence from previously circulating H5N1 viruses. G2-EC viruses accumulated a characteristic set of hemagglutinin amino acid substitutions, most of which were located in antigenic regions. Across the clade 2.3.4.4b H5 virus population, the estimated mean HA evolutionary rate was higher during 2024-2025 than during preceding periods. These genetic changes were accompanied by marked antigenic divergence from the Re14 vaccine strain, with 4- to 32-fold reductions in HI titres. Genomic analysis revealed acquisition of PB1 segment from a distinct genetic background in G2-EC H5N1 viruses, followed by the emergence of H5N6 viruses sharing a highly similar genetic backbone but carrying a distinct NA segment, indicating sequential reassortment. Animal experiments showed that representative G2-EC viruses retained high pathogenicity and efficient direct-contact transmission in SPF chickens, while exhibiting relatively limited lethality in mice. Collectively, these findings document a recent evolutionary transition of clade 2.3.4.4b H5 viruses in China, characterized by genetic and antigenic divergence accompanied by sequential reassortment, underscoring the need for continued genomic and antigenic surveillance.
abstract_zh: 进化枝2.3.4.4b H5病毒自在中国出现以来经历了连续的进化,但最近流行的病毒的遗传和抗原多样性程度仍不清楚。在这里,我们对 2024 年至 2025 年期间在中国通过常规 监测 分离的 18 种 H5 病毒进行了特征分析,以及自 2020 年以来收集的公开的进化枝 2.3.4.4b H5 序列。系统发育分析表明,这些分离株在进化枝 2.3.4.4b 内形成了一个独特的进化簇,称为 G2 衍生的新兴簇 (G2-EC),于 2024 年中期左右出现,与之前流行的 H5N1 病毒表现出明显的遗传差异。G2-EC病毒积累了一组特征性的血凝素氨基酸取代,其中大部分位于抗原区域。在分支 2.3.4.4b H5 病毒群体中,2024-2025 年期间估计的平均 HA 进化率高于之前时期。这些基因变化伴随着与 Re14 疫苗 菌株的显着抗原差异,HI 滴度降低了 4 至 32 倍。基因组分析显示,G2-EC H5N1 病毒从不同的遗传背景中获得了 PB1 片段,随后出现了共享高度相似的遗传主链但携带不同 NA 片段的 H5N6 病毒,这表明存在连续重配。动物实验表明,代表性的G2-EC病毒在SPF鸡中保留了高致病性和高效的直接接触传播,而在小鼠中表现出相对有限的致死率。总的来说,这些发现记录了中国分支 2.3.4.4b H5 病毒最近的进化转变,其特征是遗传和抗原分歧伴随着顺序重配,强调了持续基因组和抗原 监测 的需要。

title: A Discrete Choice Experiment to Explore Drivers of Mask-Wearing
abstract: A discrete choice experiment will examine how disease factors, policy, and social factors influence mask-wearing decisions during a hypothetical bird flu outbreak. Specifically, it will explore the influence of five different factors (infection rate, mortality rate, mask mandate, social norm, presence of vulnerable others) on individuals’ decision to wear a medical mask. Due to recent outbreaks of bird flu among livestock across the US, many health professionals are concerned about the potential of the bird flu virus to mutate leading to a large outbreak among humans. Therefore, we designed our study asking participants to report how likely they would be to wear a mask in different scenarios during such a hypothetical outbreak of bird flu.

title: Global monitoring of wildlife mortality through participatory science in near‐real time
abstract: Detection of wildlife mortality events is critical for timely conservation and natural resource management. We present an open‐source, web‐based, decision‐support tool that queries, aggregates, and summarizes participatory‐science data from iNaturalist to monitor mortality events worldwide. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach using four case studies spanning taxonomic, spatial, and temporal scales. In Canada and the US, high peaks of bird mortality coincided with zoonotic risk during avian influenza outbreaks. Across Africa, we detected 45 mortality events of threatened species in March 2026. In California, recorded mammal mortality was associated with human infrastructure, including proximity to roads, and to a lesser extent, the human footprint. Mortality of pumas ( Puma concolor ) was detected across 12 countries, highlighting the need for international cooperation to conserve mobile species. Our tool enables resource managers to flag emerging threats and empowers participatory scientists to monitor and integrate mortality records for conservation.
journal: Frontiers in Ecology and the Environment

title: Cross-Protection against Influenza A(H5) Clade 2.3.4.4b Viruses after A(H1N1)pdm09 Infection.
abstract: We challenged ferrets previously infected with influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus with H5N1 or H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses to assess cross-protection. Results show that previous A(H1N1)pdm09 virus immunity conferred partial protection against both viruses, with slightly reduced protection against H5N5 compared with H5N1, potentially reflecting the absence of cross-reactive N5 neuraminidase antibodies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess whether prior infection with influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus provides cross-protection against H5N1 and H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses, addressing a knowledge gap about immune responses to avian influenza subtypes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved challenging ferrets previously infected with influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus with H5N1 and H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses to evaluate cross-protection in an animal model.
analysis.methods: Ferrets were infected with influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus and then challenged with H5N1 or H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses to assess immune responses and viral replication.
analysis.main_results: Results showed that previous A(H1N1)pdm09 virus immunity conferred partial protection against both H5N1 and H5N5 viruses, with slightly reduced protection against H5N5 compared to H5N1, potentially due to the absence of cross-reactive N5 neuraminidase antibodies.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that immunity from A(H1N1)pdm09 infection may offer some cross-protection against H5N1 and H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses, highlighting the potential for immune cross-reactivity in avian influenza subtypes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results may inform surveillance and risk assessment strategies for avian influenza subtypes, particularly in understanding immune responses and potential cross-protection in human populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to an animal model, and the evidence is based on a single challenge experiment, which may not fully represent human immune responses. The evidence is moderate in strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether prior infection with influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus provides cross-protection against H5N1 and H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses. Ferrets previously infected with A(H1N1)pdm09 were challenged with these avian influenza subtypes to assess immune responses. Results indicated partial protection against both viruses, with slightly reduced protection against H5N5, possibly due to the absence of cross-reactive N5 neuraminidase antibodies. The findings suggest that immunity from A(H1N1)pdm09 infection may offer some cross-protection against H5N1 and H5N5 viruses, which could have implications for understanding immune responses to avian influenza subtypes. However, the study is limited to an animal model and relies on a single challenge experiment, which may not fully reflect human immunity. The evidence is moderate in strength.

title: Assessment of Biosecurity Measures in Live Poultry Markets in N’Djamena, Chad
abstract: Background and Objective: Although, biosecurity is a primary means of disease prevention in livestock farming, implementing these measures remains challenging in live poultry supply chains. This study evaluated the implementation of biosecurity measures across four major commercial markets in N'Djamena, Chad: Al-Afia, Champs de Fil, Diguel and Dembé. Methodology: Between July and August 2023, a cross-sectional survey was conducted among 120 permanent live poultry vendors. A structured questionnaire was used to assess vendors' awareness of avian pathogens, knowledge of biosecurity standards and implementation of sanitary practices. Results: The results showed that 60.83% of vendors had low levels of biosecurity knowledge, 23.34% had moderate knowledge and 15.83% had good knowledge. Dembé market had the highest proportion of vendors with good biosecurity knowledge, with 6.67% of the total respondents classified in this category and a Mean±SD of 6.67±0.97%, significantly higher than the corresponding values for Al-Afia (2.50±0.31%) and Diguel (1.66±0.09%). Regarding compliance, 60% of vendors failed to implement biosecurity protocols, whereas only 5% adhered strictly to the recommended standards. Complete non-implementation was most prevalent at Diguel (17.50±4.28%) and Al-Afia (15.00±3.44%), compared with Champs de Fil (10.83±2.87%). These deficiencies were associated with a lack of formal training, inadequate market infrastructure and low perceived immediate health risks. Conclusion: The findings indicate substantial gaps in biosecurity knowledge and compliance among live poultry vendors in N'Djamena. Given the potential role of live poultry markets in the transmission of avian influenza, Newcastle disease and other infectious diseases, targeted training programs, infrastructure improvements and strengthened regulatory frameworks are urgently needed.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估乍得恩贾梅纳活家禽市场生物安全措施的实施情况,因为生物安全是畜牧业疾病预防的主要手段,但这些措施在活家禽供应链中仍然具有挑战性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对乍得恩贾梅纳四个主要商业市场(Al-Afia、Champs de Fil、Diguel 和 Dembé)的 120 个固定活家禽供应商进行了横断面调查。
elements_zh.methods: 2023 年 7 月至 8 月期间,使用结构化调查问卷评估供应商对禽类病原体的认识、生物安全标准的了解以及卫生实践的实施情况。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果显示,60.83%的商户生物安全知识水平较低,23.34%的商户生物安全知识水平一般,15.83%的商户生物安全知识水平较高。Dembé 市场拥有良好生物安全知识的供应商比例最高,占受访者总数的 6.67%,Mean±SD 为 6.67±0.97%,显着高于 Al-Afia(2.50±0.31%)和 Diguel(1.66±0.09%)的相应值。在合规性方面,60% 的供应商未能实施生物安全协议,而只有 5% 的供应商严格遵守建议的标准。与 Champs de Fil (10.83±2.87%) 相比,完全不执行的情况在 Diguel (17.50±4.28%) 和 Al-Afia (15.00±3.44%) 最为普遍。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 调查结果表明,恩贾梅纳的活家禽供应商在生物安全知识和合规性方面存在巨大差距,凸显了有针对性的培训计划、基础设施改进和强化监管框架的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究深入了解了活禽市场的生物安全实践,这对于预防 传播 和其他传染病至关重要,并强调了改进这些实践以保障公众健康的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其横截面设计和对自我报告数据的依赖而受到限制,这可能会引入偏差。证据是温和的,因为它是基于调查结果而不是直接的生物学或临床测量。

abstract_zh: 背景和目标:尽管生物安全是畜牧业疾病预防的主要手段,但在活家禽供应链中实施这些措施仍然具有挑战性。这项研究评估了乍得恩贾梅纳四个主要商业市场(Al-Afia、Champs de Fil、Diguel 和 Dembé)生物安全措施的实施情况。方法:2023 年 7 月至 8 月期间,对 120 个固定活家禽摊贩进行了横断面调查。使用结构化调查问卷来评估供应商对禽类病原体的认识、生物安全标准的知识和卫生实践的实施情况。结果:结果显示,60.83%的商贩生物安全知识水平较低,23.34%的商户生物安全知识中等,15.83%的商户生物安全知识良好。Dembé 市场拥有良好生物安全知识的供应商比例最高,占受访者总数的 6.67%,Mean±SD 为 6.67±0.97%,显着高于 Al-Afia(2.50±0.31%)和 Diguel(1.66±0.09%)的相应值。在合规性方面,60% 的供应商未能实施生物安全协议,而只有 5% 的供应商严格遵守建议的标准。与 Champs de Fil (10.83±2.87%) 相比,完全不执行的情况在 Diguel (17.50±4.28%) 和 Al-Afia (15.00±3.44%) 最为普遍。这些缺陷与缺乏正规培训、市场基础设施不足以及对直接健康风险的认识较低有关。结论:调查结果表明恩贾梅纳活家禽供应商在生物安全知识和合规性方面存在巨大差距。鉴于活禽市场在新城疫和其他传染病中的潜在作用,迫切需要有针对性的培训计划、基础设施改善和强化监管框架。

title: Legal Approaches advancing One health
abstract: This paper examines the development of the One Health approach at global and European Union (EU) levels, arguing that a regulatory perspective is essential for its effective implementation. Following a brief introduction, Paragraph II outlines the historical evolution of One Health, showing its progression from a predominantly sanitary concept to one that fully incorporates environmental dimensions. Paragraph III analyses the contribution of international organizations in promoting and operationalizing the approach. Paragraph IV discusses the role of legislation in institutionalizing One Health and reviews different legal pathways – ranging from its recognition as a general legal principle to its integration into sector specific legislation and the adoption of a comprehensive framework law – illustrated with examples from EU laws and policies. Paragraph V presents concrete instances of how One Health has been incorporated into legal systems, particularly in the areas of avian influenza, biodiversity conservation and agri-food systems, again drawing on EU regulation. The paper concludes that no single legal model can universally operationalize One Health; rather, the choice of regulatory approach must be adapted to the specific policy priorities and institutional context of each country or forum.

abstract_zh: 本文探讨了“同一个健康”方法在全球和欧盟 (EU) 层面的发展,认为监管视角对于其有效实施至关重要。在简要介绍之后,第二段概述了 One Health 的历史 进化,展示了其从主要卫生概念到完全融入环境维度的概念的进展。第三段分析了国际组织在促进和实施该方法方面的贡献。第四段讨论了立法在“统一健康”制度化中的作用,并回顾了不同的法律途径——从将其视为一项一般法律原则到将其纳入具体部门的立法以及采用全面的框架法——并以欧盟法律和政策的例子进行说明。第五段介绍了如何将“同一个健康”纳入法律体系的具体实例,特别是在 禽流感、生物多样性保护和农业食品系统领域,再次借鉴欧盟法规。该文件的结论是,没有任何单一的法律模式可以普遍实施“同一个健康”;相反,监管方法的选择必须适应每个国家或论坛的具体政策优先事项和体制背景。

title: Knowledge, Attitude, and Practices Regarding One Health and Zoonotic Diseases Among Undergraduate Medical Students at a Tertiary Care Hospital in Assam, India: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Background Zoonotic diseases are a major public health concern in Northeast India, and future physicians need One Health competencies to control them. We assessed One Health and zoonosis-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) among MBBS students. Methodology This cross-sectional study (September 11 to October 11, 2026) used an attempted census of MBBS students across all three phases (Phase I, Phase II, and Phase III, the last comprising Part I and Part II) at Gauhati Medical College and Hospital, Assam. A pilot-tested online questionnaire assessed knowledge (20 items), attitude, and practice (15 items each); scores ≥80% (modified Bloom’s cut-offs) indicated good knowledge, positive attitude, or good practice. Kruskal-Wallis, chi-square, and multivariable logistic regression were used for data analysis. Results Of the 881 eligible students, 512 (58.1%) responded (median age = 20 years; interquartile range = 19-21 years; 333 (65.0%) male); only 37 (7.2%) had previous One Health training. Good knowledge, positive attitude, and good practice were found in 352 (68.8%), 269 (52.5%), and 323 (63.1%) students, respectively. Knowledge was lowest for brucellosis (286, 55.9%), Nipah virus (331, 64.6%), and avian influenza (333, 65.0%). Protective practices were common, but fewer than half often or always attended seminars (243, 47.5%) or awareness activities (253, 49.4%). All domains differed significantly by phase: good knowledge and practice were highest in Phase III Part II (103, 86.6% and 89, 74.8%), and lowest in Phase II (68, 50.7% and 74, 55.2%), whereas positive attitude was highest in Phase I (134, 66.3%). Compared to Phase I, Phase III Part II students had higher odds of good knowledge (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 2.63, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.39-4.99) and good practice (aOR = 1.81, 1.06-3.08; practice model p = 0.057), while all later phases had lower odds of positive attitude (aOR = 0.28-0.51). title: Rising biosecurity threats: Insights from Queensland’s approach to advancing response readiness
abstract: Effective biosecurity is a growing global challenge, rapidly escalating in scale, complexity, cost, and consequence. Best-practice biosecurity seeks to protect people, animals, and the environment from exotic pests and diseases, yet ensuring a resilient response framework remains difficult, even in geographically remote countries such as Australia. Biosecurity incidents are an underappreciated security risk, increasing in both frequency and intensity within an era of polycrisis, where climate variability, natural disasters, geopolitical instability, disrupted supply chains, food insecurity, pandemics, and economic volatility interact and amplify impacts. Drawing on a government practitioner perspective, this paper argues that biosecurity must be understood as a disaster resilience issue rather than solely an agricultural one. Using examples including red imported fire ants and preparedness for highly pathogenic avian influenza, it highlights how biological threats increasingly intersect with public health, environmental management, emergency preparedness, and community resilience. The paper demonstrates the importance of early detection, cross-sector coordination, surge capability, institutional adaptability, and sustained community engagement. Industries, governments, and communities all play critical roles in preventing, identifying, and responding to biosecurity threats. Advancing response readiness requires stronger partnerships, trusted networks, and governance arrangements capable of managing escalating biological risks in an increasingly complex, interconnected, and uncertain operating environment. This article is also included in The Business & Management Collection which can be accessed at https://hstalks.com/business/.
journal: Journal of Business Continuity & Emergency Planning

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the growing global challenge of effective biosecurity, particularly in the context of avian influenza A viruses, avian-origin zoonotic infections, and their subtypes. The central question is how to enhance response readiness to these biological threats, considering their increasing frequency and intensity in an era of polycrisis. The scope includes examining biosecurity as a disaster resilience issue, not solely an agricultural one, and highlights the need for cross-sector coordination, early detection, and community engagement.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on a government practitioner perspective, drawing on examples such as red imported fire ants and preparedness for highly pathogenic avian influenza. It does not report on specific databases, search dates, or eligibility criteria. The methods section emphasizes the importance of early detection, cross-sector coordination, surge capability, institutional adaptability, and sustained community engagement as key components of a resilient biosecurity framework.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that biosecurity incidents are an underappreciated security risk, increasing in both frequency and intensity due to the interactions of multiple global crises. It highlights that biological threats increasingly intersect with public health, environmental management, emergency preparedness, and community resilience. The paper demonstrates the importance of early detection, cross-sector coordination, surge capability, institutional adaptability, and sustained community engagement in managing these risks.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies a lack of emphasis on biosecurity as a disaster resilience issue rather than an agricultural one. It also notes that while the importance of early detection and cross-sector coordination is acknowledged, there is a gap in understanding how these strategies can be effectively implemented in an increasingly complex and interconnected operating environment. Additionally, the review does not provide detailed evidence on the effectiveness of specific interventions or the extent of their application across different regions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that advancing response readiness requires stronger partnerships, trusted networks, and governance arrangements capable of managing escalating biological risks. It highlights the need for sustained community engagement and institutional adaptability. Furthermore, it calls for a more integrated approach to biosecurity that considers its intersection with public health, environmental management, and emergency preparedness.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the growing global challenge of effective biosecurity, particularly in the context of avian influenza A viruses and related zoonotic infections. It argues that biosecurity must be understood as a disaster resilience issue, not solely an agricultural one, and highlights the need for cross-sector coordination, early detection, and community engagement. The paper demonstrates the importance of institutional adaptability and surge capability in managing escalating biological risks. While it provides general insights into the increasing frequency and intensity of biosecurity threats, it does not offer detailed evidence on the effectiveness of specific interventions. The review calls for stronger partnerships and governance arrangements to enhance response readiness in an increasingly complex and uncertain environment.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注有效生物安全方面日益严峻的全球挑战,特别是在 禽流感 A 病毒、禽源人畜共患感染及其亚型的背景下。核心问题是,考虑到在多重危机时代这些生物威胁的频率和强度不断增加,如何加强对这些生物威胁的应对准备。范围包括将生物安全视为一个抗灾问题,而不仅仅是农业问题,并强调跨部门协调、早期发现和社区参与的必要性。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查基于政府从业者的角度,借鉴了红火蚁和 高致病性禽流感 的准备等例子。它不报告特定数据库、检索日期或资格标准。方法部分强调了早期发现、跨部门协调、激增能力、机构适应性和持续社区参与作为弹性生物安全框架关键组成部分的重要性。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,生物安全事件是一种被低估的安全风险,由于多种全球危机的相互作用,其频率和强度都在增加。它强调生物威胁日益与公共卫生、环境管理、应急准备和社区复原力相互交叉。该文件论证了早期发现、跨部门协调、激增能力、机构适应性和持续社区参与在管理这些风险方面的重要性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查指出,生物安全缺乏作为抗灾问题而不是农业问题的重视。报告还指出,虽然早期发现和跨部门协调的重要性已得到承认,但在理解如何在日益复杂和相互关联的运营环境中有效实施这些策略方面存在差距。此外,该审查没有提供具体干预措施的有效性或其在不同地区的应用程度的详细证据。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 审查表明,推进应对准备工作需要更强有力的伙伴关系、值得信赖的网络和能够管理不断升级的生物风险的治理安排。它强调了持续社区参与和机构适应性的必要性。此外,它呼吁采取更加综合的生物安全方法,考虑其与公共卫生、环境管理和应急准备的交叉点。

abstract_zh: 有效的生物安全是一项日益严峻的全球挑战,其规模、复杂性、成本和后果迅速升级。最佳实践生物安全旨在保护人类、动物和环境免受外来病虫害的侵害,但确保有弹性的应对框架仍然很困难,即使在澳大利亚等地理位置偏远的国家也是如此。生物安全事件是一种被低估的安全风险,在多重危机时代,其频率和强度都在增加,气候变化、自然灾害、地缘政治不稳定、供应链中断、粮食不安全、流行病和经济波动相互作用并放大影响。本文从政府从业者的角度出发,认为生物安全必须被理解为一个抗灾问题,而不仅仅是一个农业问题。它以红火蚁和 高致病性禽流感 的防备为例,强调了生物威胁如何与公共卫生、环境管理、应急准备和社区复原力日益交叉。该文件论证了早期发现、跨部门协调、激增能力、机构适应性和持续社区参与的重要性。行业、政府和社区在预防、识别和应对生物安全威胁方面都发挥着关键作用。推进应对准备工作需要更强有力的伙伴关系、可信网络和治理安排,以便能够在日益复杂、相互关联和不确定的运营环境中管理不断升级的生物风险。本文还包含在《商业与管理合集》中,可通过 https://hstalks.com/business/ 访问。

analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,生物安全事件是一种被低估的安全风险,由于多种全球危机的相互作用,其频率和强度都在增加。它强调生物威胁日益与公共卫生、环境管理、应急准备和社区复原力相互交叉。该文件论证了早期发现、跨部门协调、激增能力、机构适应性和持续社区参与在管理这些风险方面的重要性。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查指出,生物安全缺乏作为抗灾问题而不是农业问题的重视。报告还指出,虽然早期发现和跨部门协调的重要性已得到承认,但在理解如何在日益复杂和相互关联的运营环境中有效实施这些策略方面存在差距。此外,该审查没有提供具体干预措施的有效性或其在不同地区的应用程度的详细证据。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 审查表明,推进应对准备工作需要更强有力的伙伴关系、值得信赖的网络和能够管理不断升级的生物风险的治理安排。它强调了持续社区参与和机构适应性的必要性。此外,它呼吁采取更加综合的生物安全方法,考虑其与公共卫生、环境管理和应急准备的交叉点。

title: Prevalence and associated factors of influenza A virus infection among patients with acute respiratory tract infections in Gondar City, Northwest Ethiopia
abstract: BACKGROUND: Influenza A virus is a major cause of acute respiratory tract infections and contributes substantially to the global disease burden. Laboratory-confirmed data on influenza A virus infection remain limited in the study area. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence of influenza A virus infection and to identify possible associated factors among patients with acute respiratory tract infections attending selected health institutions in Gondar City, Northwest Ethiopia. METHODS: A multi-center, health facility-based cross-sectional study was carried out from January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025. In total, 490 patients with acute respiratory tract infections were enrolled from five health facilities in Gondar City. Demographic, behavioral, and clinical information was collected using a structured questionnaire. Nasopharyngeal swabs were collected and tested for influenza A virus using multiplex real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). Logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with influenza A virus infection. RESULTS: Influenza A virus was detected in 65 of the 490 participants, with an overall prevalence of 13.3% (95% CI: 10.3-16.3). Among the confirmed cases, 48 (73.8%) were A(H1N1) and 17 (26.2%) were A(H3N2). In multivariable logistic regression, participants aged 5-17 years (AOR: 3.14; 95% CI: 1.36-7.25; p = 0.008) and 18-49 years (AOR: 3.50; 95% CI: 1.54-7.20; p = 0.002) had higher odds of infection than those aged <5 years. Secondary education was associated with lower odds of infection compared with no formal education (AOR: 0.07; 95% CI: 0.01-0.75; p = 0.029), while employed participants had higher odds than students (AOR: 3.54; 95% CI: 1.47-7.80; p = 0.028). CONCLUSION: Influenza A virus infection was detected among patients presenting with acute respiratory tract infections in Gondar City, highlighting the importance of influenza surveillance and laboratory confirmation in this population. Strengthening routine molecular surveillance, promoting seasonal influenza vaccination among high-risk populations, reinforcing infection prevention and control measures, and implementing targeted community health education are essential to improve influenza prevention and control.

full_text: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (H5N1 bird flu) is the defining disease of our times, suggests Australian writer and journalist Michael Dulaney in his timely book Sentinels, on what happens when diseases spread between animals and humans. Now impacting mainland Australian wildlife, the disease, which reached us in June, epitomises our callous neglect of nature, despite us being embedded in and reliant on it. “Of all the pathogens I’ve learned about, this is the big one,” Dulaney writes. Review: Sentinels by Michael Dulaney (Scribe Publications) Over 700 bird flu events – which cover individual or multiple deaths of animals – have occurred in Australia so far. Greater crested terns, little penguins, common bottlenose dolphin, long-nosed fur seals, Australian sea lions, and many other bird and mammal species have all succumbed. It’s a sobering result of our missed chances to protect nature and prevent pathogens from jumping between non-human animals and people. In his book, which was longlisted for this year’s Walkley Book Award and published just a few months after bird flu reached Australia, Dulaney thoughtfully discusses our impacts on and connections with non-human life. We continue to exploit species and plunder nature at an alarming scale and rate. It’s estimated humans exploit as much as 300 times more species than non-human predators. The concept of a sentinel — the canary in the coal mine — draws from epidemiology, the study of disease. Dulaney’s thesis is that these sentinels are increasingly sickly, often dropping dead at disturbingly regular rates and in extraordinary numbers. It’s hard to dispute this. A recent grisly example is the estimated death of more than 13,000 elephant seal pups, more than 75% of all pups born, on the sub-Antarctic Heard Island last summer, as their remote, isolated location and shielding from H5N1 bird flu were inevitably breached. Humans are destroying nature and the spillover of diseases that jump between species – including to and from humans – is increasing. Dulaney writes: Researchers have counted around 200 new infectious diseases that have broken out more than 12,000 times over the past three decades On average, one new infectious disease jumps to humans every eight months. He suggests this threat should be considered in the same way as other globally significant and existential threats, including climate change. As a wildlife ecologist and conservation scientist, I echo his call to action. A joy to read Sentinels is composed of three parts and eight chapters. The first part is focused on wildlife, the second on agriculture and the third looks at the impacts of commerce, the wildlife trade and our treatment of fellow human beings. One chilling passage describes how in California’s bulging prison population, one of five of the state’s cases of Valley fever (a disease caused by pathogenic fungi) was found among its prisoners between 2007 and 2011. Dulaney’s writing is a joy. Easily consumed, complex ideas and information are made accessible to the reader. Sentinels is very well referenced too, including extensive peer-reviewed research. Case studies span China, the Andes, the Arctic, Indonesia, Australia and elsewhere. As a result, this book is undoubtedly globally relevant. Dulaney also takes his readers to the front lines. There are stories of ecologists studying flying foxes in forests, and about the relevance of Hendra virus, which causes severe, often fatal disease in both infected horses and humans. It can pass from bats to horses, and has killed people working with horses. Elsewhere, the book details people trying to protect endangered amphibians on Indonesian mountains, as Dulaney spends four days with Angga, a gifted wildlife tracker. “Sometimes, when Angga uncovers an exceptionally rare frog or snake species, his clients break down crying over finding something they have searched for their whole lives,” he writes. There’s even discussion of the potential links between pigs, East Germany and the fall of communism. The epilogue is perhaps the most powerful and vital section of the book. It brings together how what’s happening is not a case of misfortune, but a predictable, likely outcome of what we’re doing: the habitats we destroy, and the crowding of people and animals. The science is clear. Our actions are stressing wildlife populations and in some cases, they bring wildlife and their diseases closer to us and the animals we farm and eat. It’s a recipe for disaster. The increasing reliance of flying foxes on urban environments to find food – and the Hendra virus risk this poses – is because we’ve destroyed large areas of forests and woodlands these animals relied upon. Dulaney comes hard at capitalism, too, pointing to its commodification of nature. This will likely rankle some – but again, it’s hard to argue against. Even within the conservation community I’m part of, the value of species and ecosystems are often framed and described through the services they provide us, rather than their intrinsic value. The Australian government now has a Nature repair market, which includes the use of controversial offsets that allow for further environmental destruction. Dulaney is clear about his ecological grief. “In the days prior to handling ducks, I’d watched distressing video compilations filmed by carers around the world who could do nothing but witness these slow deaths,” he writes about bird flu. In the chapter devoted to it, he writes: I have come to believe that bird flu is the archetypal disease of this new age, the one that represents all of our failed efforts to address the growing threat of spillover – a disease that links farming, unrestrained industry, political intransigience, and environmental exploitation in a way that threatens hundreds of species, including our own. It scares me more than anything else. His honesty and authenticity mean Sentinels rises above many science-based books I’ve read, which clumsily attempt to hide the authors’ personal views and values. We are not impartial automatons: we all have skin in this game, which concerns our only home. Dulaney makes the case for urgent and substantial change. Hope, but no sugarcoating Much of the book is confronting; Dulaney does not sugarcoat our predicament. But he offers hope – and makes the important point that tackling disease will also help address other crises, such as climate change, which are inextricably linked. Sentinels covers a lot of ground. Given the complexities of disease ecology and the wicked problem of managing wildlife and societies to reduce our exposure to pandemics and better protect biodiversity, it’s unsurprising some issues aren’t covered in the depth I might desire. But in my view, this is more than compensated for by the broad knowledge and understanding readers will get from Dulaney’s book. Sentinels is a vital read. I hope it reaches a diverse audience, including our political leaders, who need to confront the challenges it so thoughtfully describes. To protect ourselves, we must protect our ecosystems and the species that sustain them. The ongoing demise of wildlife and the global rise of diseases and pandemics sound clarion calls we must urgently act upon. We must improve our relationship with nature.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study highlights the growing threat of avian influenza A viruses, particularly H5N1 bird flu, as a defining disease of our times, emphasizing the need to address the increasing spillover of pathogens between animals and humans.

analysis.methods: The methods involve a narrative review of the book, analyzing case studies and examples of avian influenza A virus outbreaks, including H5N1, in different regions and species, and discussing the ecological and societal factors contributing to disease spillover.
analysis.main_results: The book reports over 700 bird flu events in Australia, with more than 13,000 elephant seal pups estimated to have died on Heard Island, and highlights the increasing frequency of zoonotic influenza outbreaks, with around 200 new infectious diseases jumping to humans over the past three decades.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Dulaney interprets these findings as a predictable outcome of human activities that destroy habitats and bring wildlife and domestic animals closer to humans, suggesting that avian influenza A viruses, particularly H5N1, represent a broader crisis of spillover diseases and environmental exploitation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for better surveillance and protection of ecosystems to reduce the risk of zoonotic influenza outbreaks, emphasizing the interconnectedness of environmental health and public health.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a book review and does not include original data or statistical analysis, which limits its evidence strength. However, it provides a comprehensive overview of the ecological and societal context of avian influenza A virus spread.

analysis.summary_en: This analysis focuses on the growing threat of avian influenza A viruses, particularly H5N1 bird flu, as highlighted in Michael Dulaney's book 'Sentinels'. The study discusses the increasing frequency of zoonotic influenza outbreaks, with over 700 bird flu events reported in Australia and more than 13,000 elephant seal pups dying on Heard Island. Dulaney argues that these events are a predictable outcome of human activities that destroy habitats and increase contact between wildlife and humans. The findings underscore the importance of protecting ecosystems to mitigate the risk of disease spillover. However, the study is based on a book review and lacks original data, which limits its evidence strength. The book serves as a call to action for addressing the interconnected crises of environmental destruction and public health threats.

title_zh: 《哨兵》是对禽流感和疯狂资本主义采取行动的紧急呼吁。读书也是一种享受
source_body_en: Review: Sentinels by Michael Dulaney (Scribe Publications) Over 700 bird flu events – which cover individual or multiple deaths of animals – have occurred in Australia so far. It’s a sobering result of our missed chances to protect nature and prevent pathogens from jumping between non-human animals and people. The concept of a sentinel — the canary in the coal mine — draws from epidemiology, the study of disease. As a result, this book is undoubtedly globally relevant. “Sometimes, when Angga uncovers an exceptionally rare frog or snake species, his clients break down crying over finding something they have searched for their whole lives,” he writes. Highly pathogenic avian influenza (H5N1 bird flu) is the defining disease of our times, suggests Australian writer and journalist Michael Dulaney in his timely book Sentinels, on what happens when diseases spread between animals and humans. Now impacting mainland Australian wildlife, the disease, which reached us in June, epitomises our callous neglect of nature, despite us being embedded in and reliant on it. “Of all the pathogens I’ve learned about, this is the big one,” Dulaney writes. Greater crested terns, little penguins, common bottlenose dolphin, long-nosed fur seals, Australian sea lions, and many other bird and mammal species have all succumbed. In his book, which was longlisted for this year’s Walkley Book Award and published just a few months after bird flu reached Australia, Dulaney thoughtfully discusses our impacts on and connections with non-human life. We continue to exploit species and plunder nature at an alarming scale and rate. It’s estimated humans exploit as much as 300 times more species than non-human predators.
